text_blocks.snippet: Yes, Medicare Part B premiums can be tax deductible for some individuals, but there are specific rules and limitations. If you itemize deductions on your federal tax return, you can include your Medicare Part B premiums as a deductible medical expense. However, you can only deduct the amount that exceeds 7.5% of your adjusted gross income (AGI).

list.title: Itemizing is Key:
list.snippet: You can only deduct Medicare Part B premiums if you itemize deductions on your tax return rather than taking the standard deduction.

list.title: AGI Threshold:
list.snippet: Your total medical expenses, including Medicare Part B premiums, must exceed 7.5% of your AGI before you can claim a deduction.

list.title: Self-Employed Individuals:
list.snippet: If you're self-employed and your business shows a profit, you can deduct your Medicare Part B premiums (and other Medicare premiums) as a business expense, even if you don't itemize.

list.title: Other Medicare Premiums:
list.snippet: In addition to Part B, you can also deduct premiums for Medicare Part A (if you have to pay for it), Part C (Medicare Advantage), and Part D (prescription drug coverage), as well as Medigap policies, if they are part of your itemized deductions or if you are self-employed.

list.title: Keep Records:
list.snippet: It's crucial to keep accurate records of all your Medicare premiums and other medical expenses to support your deduction.
